$why: Columns and tables that exist in a live store and that no committed DDL
creates. Every one was an ALTER run by hand against a database, so a store
rebuilt from source is a DIFFERENT database from the one in production --
which is how the volume ended up 14 migrations behind the laptop without
anything noticing until the census read a column that was not there.
This is a DEBT LIST, not a permission list. ETL/schema/check_store_schema.py
fails on anything not recorded here, and fails again once an entry stops
being true, so the only direction it can move is down. Clearing an entry
means writing its migration into ETL/events/load/migrations/ and lowering
'budget' is the count of entries below. It is stated separately on purpose:
